commit.message:
feat(edm): wire EDM 4-axis - upper and lower profiles paired into rulings by a stated rule

A Wire Contour's four_axis block reads the selection as two flat
profiles (the upper on the top plane, the lower on the bottom plane)
and pairs them into rulings by normalised arc length from the start
hole or by sync points; each move ends on a ruling's lower point and
its pose is the wire toward the upper point (#290 D2).

Refused by name: crossed, doubled, unpaired or off-profile sync points,
a folding or self-crossing pairing, open or mismatched profiles, a
ruling past edm.max_taper_deg, profiles off the op's planes, and a
twist that needs more than the stated tolerance - a straight wire
cannot touch a twisted ruled surface along its whole height, so the
offset is widened on both planes until the leaning kerf stands clear
at every height read, and the note says what stands for it.

The verify reads the poses as it reads a taper's; the machine check's
U/V and guide refusals apply unchanged; the wire post writes the same
taper_on / uv / taper_off codes under PARAM WireFourAxis.

Fixes #537

test(edm): pin the 4-axis wire cut's stamp, refusals and post codes

M3's safety review of PR #1181 (items 2-7) found lines a mutation could
delete with every suite still passing. Each now has a test that fails
when its line is removed:

- wire_stamp: the 4-axis block's pairing rule, each sync point on each
  side, and the tolerance each move the stamp; a one-profile cut's
  stamp is pinned to main's value; the machine's max_taper_deg moves a
  4-axis cut's stamp (stamp_condition).
- wire_4axis: a 4-axis cut with a no-core burnout is refused by name;
  a 4-axis cut posted on a machine missing taper_on, taper_off or uv is
  refused by the wire post by name.
- motion ruled_tests: a pairing whose offset wire folds (the second
  fold law) and a lead whose leaning kerf enters the paired surface are
  each refused by name.

Refs #537
